The *Atītavāra* ("Section on the Past", Ya 10.3.2) is a canonical Abhidhamma text located within the *Yamaka* [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. Belonging to the tenth major division of the work (the *Indriyayamaka*), this section applies the characteristic Yamaka method of paired, logically exhaustive catechisms to analyze psychological phenomena and spiritual faculties specifically in relation to the past [Catalog; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language for this text [SuttaCentral]. None of the available secondary literature passages directly discuss this specific section, as all matched references merely invoke the generic term *atīta* in narrative or philosophical contexts.

According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the *Atītavāra* exhibits extensive internal text reuse across the *Yamaka*, reflecting the highly formulaic structure of the Abhidhamma's temporal divisions [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual parallels occur within adjacent subsections of the same chapter, most notably *Uppādavāra* (Ya 10.2.1; 700 matches), *Paccuppannātītavāra* (Ya 10.3.4; 310 matches), *Atītānāgatavāra* (Ya 10.3.6; 323 matches), *Anāgatavāra* (Ya 10.3.3; 205 matches), and *Paccuppannavāra* (Ya 10.3.1; 173 matches) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares recurring diagnostic formulas with homonymous *Atītavāra* sections in other chapters (Ya 2.3.2 and Ya 3.3.2) and is cited in the Abhidhamma subcommentary *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
